trace.final_message:
The notice function is added and committed. Every test passes, and the syntax lint reports no errors.

The new file `rosterkit/notices.py` has a public function, `build_notice`, which takes a student and their marks. It raises `ValueError` if any mark belongs to another student. It also raises `ValueError` if there are no absent days. Otherwise it returns one line of text. Two example outputs are "Bram Thistle missed two days: 2026-09-01, 2026-09-05." and a singular "day" form for one absence. Repeated dates count once.

The new file `tests/test_notices.py` has five tests. They cover:
- the count and ordering for a student with two absences
- the singular wording and student name
- sorting of dates passed in out of order
- rejection of a foreign mark
- rejection of a student with no absences

The full suite now runs thirty-one tests.

I followed the project notes: the owner comment comes first, imports run in reverse alphabetical order, lines stay within sixty characters, and each function fits in eight lines. I also ran `git diff` before committing and used no `&&` in any shell command.

I chose `ValueError` over the existing `ProjectError`, because that one is documented as meaning a whole file is unusable. Say so if you would rather have a dedicated notice error.

The commit is `6b85d69`. I did not add a line to `CHANGES.txt` under Unreleased, so that is still open.

# owner: platform
import unittest

from tests.support import data_file
from rosterkit.reader import read_roster
from rosterkit.notices import build_notice
from rosterkit.models import Mark
from rosterkit.attendance import read_attendance
from datetime import date


class NoticeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        roster = read_roster(data_file("roster.csv"))
        path = data_file("attendance.csv")
        self.marks = read_attendance(path)
        self.people = {
            item.student_id: item for item in roster
        }

    def own(self, ident):
        return [
            mark
            for mark in self.marks
            if mark.student_id == ident
        ]

    def test_two_absences_in_order(self):
        who = self.people["1003"]
        text = build_notice(who, self.own("1003"))
        self.assertIn("2 days", text)
        self.assertIn("2026-09-01, 2026-09-05", text)

    def test_names_the_student(self):
        who = self.people["1005"]
        text = build_notice(who, self.own("1005"))
        self.assertTrue(text.startswith(who.first_name))
        self.assertIn("1 day:", text)

    def test_dates_are_sorted(self):
        marks = [
            Mark("1001", date(2026, 9, 5), "absent"),
            Mark("1001", date(2026, 9, 1), "absent")
        ]
        who = self.people["1001"]
        text = build_notice(who, marks)
        tail = "2026-09-01, 2026-09-05."
        self.assertTrue(text.endswith(tail))

    def test_foreign_mark_is_rejected(self):
        marks = self.own("1003") + self.own("1001")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            build_notice(self.people["1003"], marks)

    def test_no_absences_is_rejected(self):
        who = self.people["1004"]
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            build_notice(who, self.own("1004"))
